problem: The backoff set is written as {0, 1, …, 2i − 1}. Without a superscript this reads as 2×i − 1, so a student would compute {0, 1, …, 5} after the third collision instead of {0, …, 7}. The exponent is missing even though the rest of the chapter uses <sup> for exponents.
fix: After the i-th collision the station picks k uniformly from {0, 1, …, 2<sup>i</sup> − 1} and waits k slot times.

problem: "it runs on every wired Ethernet LAN" is an overstatement. A modern switched, full-duplex Ethernet link has no shared medium, so CSMA/CD is not used there. The Beyond box later says exactly this, so the lead contradicts the chapter.
fix: Say that CSMA/CD shaped classic shared-cable Ethernet and CSMA/CA runs on Wi-Fi, and that today's switched full-duplex Ethernet no longer needs CSMA/CD.

problem: Exponent notation switches between <sup> (e<sup>−2G</sup>, 2<sup>i</sup>) and caret shorthand (2^i, 2i). On a phone the caret form is easy to misread as multiplication.
fix: Use <sup> everywhere: 2<sup>i</sup>, e<sup>−G</sup>, so the backoff range and the trap "not 2i and not 1 to 2^i" are written the same way as the formulas.
